body: ### Contributing guidelines - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch ### Module(s) mini.ai ### Neovim version 0.11.x ### Description When using the "a$" textobject in a context where there is a string delimited by '$'s, the first '$' isn't captured in the textobject (it should be). So for example, putting the cursor inside the dollar signs in "$asdsf$" and doing the command "da$" deletes everything except a single dollar sign. The convention for "around" textobjects is that both delimiters are included. The current behavior doesn't adhere to that convention. Most inconvenient when working in something like latex or typst where putting stuff inside '$'s is very common. `MiniAi.gen_spec.pair()` can be used to work wround this. ### Reproduction 1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory: - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows 2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'. Populate it with the following content: ```lua -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed) vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw') local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim' local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path } vim.fn.system(clone_cmd) vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw') -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim') require('mini.deps').setup() -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub ``` 3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro"). Wait for all dependencies to install. 4. Replace this with description of interactive reproduction steps along with the behavior you observe. Feel free to include images/videos/etc, this helps a lot. Use the following config (just the minimal config to set up mini.ai): ```lua -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed) vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw') local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim' local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path } vim.fn.system(clone_cmd) vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw') -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim') require('mini.deps').setup() -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub require("mini.ai").setup() ``` Edit a new buffer, and put a (possibly empty) string with a '$' at the beginning and at the end of it. comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> The convention for "around" textobjects is that both delimiters are included. The current behavior doesn't adhere to that convention.

That is not necessarily true. Selecting only one of the delimiters is an expected behavior of 'mini.ai' default textobject. It is designed to [treat input characters as a separators](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9990c41f10f54f29a888d13024c9f765037bde23/doc/mini-ai.txt#L174-L176) and not "enclosing" character. For this reason only the right edge is included by default.

This default behavior allows for a more straightforward "delete part between separators" case. The logic here is that the "enclosing" characters usually either have different left/right parts or are balanced. Which is not true for default fallback (when the character is unknown for 'mini.ai' and the user).

This behavior was initially modeled after ['wellle/targets.vim'](https://github.com/wellle/targets.vim) which is a pretty established plugin. At least to the point of having a say in what is the convention here.

> `MiniAi.gen_spec.pair()` can be used to work wround this.

Yes, this is an expected workflow here. Or via explicit textobject specification, since this should be pretty straightforward in this case. I would also suggest to set this only for filetypes where you'd use it the most (like for LaTeX in this case).

So a file '~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/plaintex.lua' with the following content should resolve the issue:

```lua
vim.b.miniai_config = {
  custom_textobjects = {
    ['$'] = { '%$().-()%$' },
  },
}
```

title: mini.ai: a$ textobject includes the last '$' in a pair, but not the first
